title: FilterBank Sinkhorn: entropic OT over the joint (image, activation) distribution
one_liner: Train with Sinkhorn divergence on the joint distribution of images and per-layer filter activations, so the cost stays finite on low-dimensional manifolds and directly penalizes a subset of filters collapsing into one oscillating mode.
description: Augment every sample with its per-layer, per-channel activation statistics and define the training cost as the Sinkhorn (entropy-regularized optimal transport) divergence between the generator's and target's distributions over this joint (image, activation) space. Sinkhorn divergence is defined and differentiable for any pair of measures — including distributions supported on low-dimensional manifolds with negligible intersection — so it removes the KL/JS/TV blow-up named in the gap, and its entropy blur keeps gradients non-vanishing as supports separate. Because the cost is a function of the joint activation distribution, a filter that collapses to a single oscillating mode creates a degenerate low-rank direction in the generator's feature distribution that the target does not have; the divergence then increases and its gradient flows specifically to that filter to re-diversify it. This differs from existing feature matching, which compares only means and cannot see subset collapse, and from image-only divergences, which cannot attribute collapse to particular filters; it extends rather than replaces the paper's own divergence by evaluating the same cost in activation space.

sections.technique: Keep the existing generator/discriminator. Add a feature extractor — either the discriminator's conv blocks or a frozen pre-trained net — and per layer global-average-pool each channel so every sample x maps to a fixed-length vector f(x) = (f_1(x), …, f_L(x)). Train with L = Sinkhorn_ε(P_gen^(joint), P_target^(joint)) on minibatches using debiased Sinkhorn iterations with a Gaussian kernel and an annealed entropy ε (optionally adding the paper's image-level cost). To test the gap-1 claim, run long training schedules and log per-filter oscillation amplitude across checkpoints, counting collapsed filters via clustering / effective rank of the activation covariance; compare against image-only divergence, mean-only feature matching, WGAN-GP, and MMD-GAN on FID, mode coverage, and # collapsed filters vs. training time. Validate the gap-2 claim on a toy task with two low-dim manifolds of negligible intersection where KL/JS/TV fail but the cost stays finite and gradients remain informative.
open_questions: Which extractor: the jointly-trained discriminator's filters (they can themselves drift or collapse, corrupting the feature coordinates) or a frozen net (whose features may not align with the generator's internal filter decomposition)?

Minibatch Sinkhorn is a biased estimator of the population divergence; does the bias grow with training length, i.e., exactly in the regime where the late-training instability appears, and does debiasing fix it?
Is the target's activation distribution genuinely non-degenerate in the coordinates that collapse? If real data is also degenerate there, the penalty would force spurious diversity.
Is the observed 'oscillating mode' really a per-sample feature-space degeneracy, or a temporal training-dynamics phenomenon that per-sample activation statistics cannot see at all?
If the paper's own divergence is not an OT-type distance, this extension may not apply — is keeping the image-level cost alongside the joint cost a second mechanism, and should it be dropped instead?
What ε schedule makes the entropy blur small enough to preserve fine-grained image structure but large enough to keep gradients on near-disjoint manifolds?
sections.rationale: Neutral stance: I took the gaps in the order that blocks progress — first a cost that is sensible on low-dim manifolds (gap 2), then used that same cost, made filter-aware, to make the remaining instability (gap 1) visible and penalizable. I did not swap the divergence or add a separate regularizer; the proposal deepens the cost by moving it into the space where the instability lives (filter activations), keeping the identity fixed. Unverified: that the underlying model is a divergence-trained convolutional GAN (the context only says 'the paper'); the finiteness and non-vanishing-gradient properties of Sinkhorn divergence for disjoint low-dim supports (standard from Genevay et al. 2018, not in context); that filter collapse to an oscillating mode is detectable as a degeneracy in per-sample activation statistics; and that the target's activation distribution is non-degenerate in the coordinates that collapse.
